Overview

About This Trip

Your journey through Lahore begins with a hotel pick-up, setting the stage for an unforgettable day exploring the city’s historical and cultural gems.

We start at the Badshahi Mosque, one of the largest and most breathtaking mosques in the world, followed by a deep dive into history at the Lahore Fort, a UNESCO World Heritage Site that showcases Mughal grandeur.

Next, we visit the Shalimar Gardens, a masterpiece of Mughal landscape design, where you can admire the symmetrical terraces, flowing fountains, and serene ambiance.

From there, we step into the past at Delhi Gate, one of the historic entrances to the Walled City of Lahore. Walking through its bustling streets, you’ll witness centuries-old architecture, vibrant bazaars, and the living history of Lahore.

A delicious authentic Lahori lunch awaits at a local restaurant, where you can indulge in the city’s famous flavors.

Our journey continues at the Lahore Museum, home to an extensive collection of artifacts, ancient manuscripts, and artistic treasures that narrate the rich heritage of the region.

As the sun begins to set, we head to the Wagah Border, where the thrilling flag-lowering ceremony between Pakistan and India takes place. This patriotic event, filled with energy and excitement, is a perfect way to end your day.

Finally, your guide will drop you back at your hotel, concluding an enriching and well-curated exploration of Lahore.

Why This Tour?

✅ Mughal Majesty – Visit Badshahi Mosque and Lahore Fort, two of the grandest Mughal-era masterpieces.
✅ Serene Landscapes – Stroll through the lush Shalimar Gardens, a UNESCO-listed masterpiece of Mughal landscaping.
✅ Walled City Wonders – Walk through Delhi Gate and explore the historic streets and bazaars of Old Lahore.
✅ Authentic Lahori Cuisine – Savor the city’s famous flavors at a top local restaurant.
✅ Cultural & Historical Insights – Discover an extensive collection of artifacts at Lahore Museum.
✅ Patriotic Spectacle – Witness the thrilling Wagah Border flag-lowering ceremony in the evening.
✅ Hassle-Free Experience – A guided tour with hotel pick-up and drop-off ensures a smooth and well-organized trip.

Itinerary

Your guide will pick you up from your hotel, and we’ll start our day exploring the cultural and historical wonders of Lahore.

Badshahi Mosque & Lahore Fort

Visit Badshahi Mosque, one of the largest and most magnificent mosques in the world, followed by a tour of the Lahore Fort, a UNESCO World Heritage Site filled with Mughal-era history.

Shalimar Gardens

Explore the stunning Shalimar Gardens, built by Emperor Shah Jahan, featuring beautiful fountains, terraces, and Mughal-style landscaping.

Delhi Gate & Walled City Exploration

Walk through Delhi Gate, one of the historic entrances to Lahore’s Walled City, and explore its vibrant streets, historical landmarks, and old bazaars.

Lunch at a Local Restaurant

Lahore Museum

Visit the Lahore Museum, home to an extensive collection of art, artifacts, and historical exhibits showcasing the region’s rich heritage.

Wagah Border – Flag-Lowering Ceremony

In the evening, we’ll head to the Wagah Border to witness the iconic flag-lowering ceremony, a patriotic and energetic display of military drills and national pride between Pakistan and India.

Drop-off at Hotel

After an exciting day exploring Lahore, your guide will drop you back at your hotel.

Key Information

  • Destinations Covered: Badshahi Mosque, Lahore Fort, Shalimar Gardens, Delhi Gate & Walled City, Lahore Museum, Wagah Border.
  • Tour Duration: Full-day tour (8-10 hours).
  • Best Season: Year-round (Winter & Spring offer the best weather).
  • Difficulty Level: Easy – Suitable for all ages, with moderate walking.
  • Starting & Ending Point: Lahore (Hotel pickup & drop-off included).
  • Entry Requirements: No special permits required; foreign travelers should carry identification.
  • Meals: Lunch at a local restaurant.
  • Transport: Private vehicle with driver and English-speaking guide.
  • Additional Costs: Entry fees (if applicable), personal expenses, and optional shopping in Walled City.
  • Customizations: Available upon request (special pickup from another city may incur additional charges).

FAQs

01

What is included in the tour?

+

The tour includes hotel pick-up and drop-off, transportation in a private vehicle, an English-speaking guide, and lunch at a local restaurant. Entry fees for the sites (if applicable) are also included.

02

How long does the tour last?

+

The tour lasts approximately 8-10 hours, depending on the pace of the group and time spent at each location.

03

Is lunch included in the tour?

+

Yes, a traditional Lahori meal is included at one of the city’s best local eateries.

04

Can I customize the tour?

+

Yes, the tour can be customized based on your preferences, such as visiting additional locations or adjusting the itinerary. Please inform us at the time of booking.

05

Do I need to bring anything with me?

+

We recommend bringing a camera, sunglasses, comfortable clothing, and walking shoes. A light shawl or scarf may be required for mosque visits.

06

Are there any age restrictions for this tour?

+

No, this tour is suitable for people of all ages. However, there may be some walking involved, so we recommend comfortable shoes.

07

Is this tour wheelchair accessible?

+

While the tour is generally accessible, some sites may have limited wheelchair access due to the nature of historical locations. Please check with us if you need specific arrangements.

08

Can I bring my children on the tour?

+
  • Yes, children are welcome! The tour is family-friendly, and we provide a relaxed pace to ensure an enjoyable experience for everyone.
09

What happens if the weather is bad?

+

The tour operates year-round, but in case of extreme weather (such as heavy rain or heat), we will modify the itinerary or reschedule the trip if necessary. We always prioritize safety and comfort.

10

What is the best time to visit Lahore?

+

The best time to visit Lahore is during the winter (November to February) and spring (March to April) when the weather is pleasant. Summer (May to August) can be very hot, especially in outdoor locations.

11

Are entry fees for the attractions included?

+

In most cases, entry fees are included for the attractions covered in the itinerary. However, some special exhibitions or areas within certain sites may have additional fees, which are not included in the tour.

12

Can I book this tour if I’m not staying in Lahore?

+

Yes, if you're traveling from another city, we can arrange special pick-up and drop-off services for an additional charge. Please contact us for more details.

Our Team

Meet the Team Behind Your

Adventure

Shah Doulat — Founder & Inspiration

Summit Experts was founded by Shah Doulat, a son of Shimshal — the legendary “Valley of Mountaineers” — whose vision and passion transformed adventure tourism in Pakistan. One of the country’s most respected high-altitude mountaineers, Shah summited some of the world’s most formidable peaks, including K2 (8,611m), Nanga Parbat (8,126m) — without supplemental oxygen — and Gasherbrum II (8,035m), alongside many other peaks and demanding treks such as Pastore Peak, Minglik Sar, the Lukpe La Trek, the Snow Lake Trek, and the K2 Base Camp & Gondogoro La Pass Trek.

But Shah measured his life by far more than summits. He believed in lifting up the next generation of guides, in safety, in professionalism, and in showing the world what local mountaineers could achieve. Though Shah is no longer with us, his spirit guides everything we do. Today, his family and the team he built and inspired carry his vision forward into every expedition we lead.

Read Shah Doulat's Full Story

Carrying His Legacy Forward

The mountaineers who lead your journey today learned the mountains alongside Shah, in the same valleys, with the same values. His own family now stands at the heart of Summit Experts — continuing his work, his standard, and his care for every traveller who joins us.

The People Who
Make It All Possible

Our team of experienced adventurers, guides, and cultural experts is here to make your journey unforgettable.

Izhar Ali

Climbing Guide

Izhar Ali is a highly skilled climbing guide with extensive experience in the Karakoram Range. He has summited Gasherbrum II (2024), the Passu Cones (2021), and Minglik Sar, showcasing his exceptional technical expertise and endurance. Known for mastering challenging passes like Verjurav La and Khurdopin La, Izhar combines a deep commitment to safety with a passion for creating unforgettable mountaineering experiences.

Yousuf Ali

Climbing Guide

An experienced climbing guide with an impressive record of high-altitude achievements. He successfully summited K2 , the world’s second-highest peak, and conquered the infamous Nanga Parbat, His ascent of Spantik Peak further highlights his technical expertise and resilience. With extensive knowledge of challenging terrains and a strong focus on safety, Yousuf ensures an exceptional mountaineering experience for every adventurer.

Tabasum Seher

Sightseeing Guide

From the breathtaking Hunza Valley, Tabasum Seher is a skilled guide specializing in Gilgit-Baltistan and Chitral Valley tours. With deep cultural knowledge and warm hospitality, she leads travelers to iconic landmarks and hidden gems, ensuring seamless and unforgettable journeys.

Samana Rahim

Mountaineer & Guide

From Shimshal Valley, Hunza, Samana Rahim is the second licensed female tourist guide in Pakistan and an accomplished mountaineer. She has guided climbs to peaks like Manglik Sar (6050m) and led an all-female team to its summit, championing women in mountaineering. With extensive trekking experience, Samana inspires adventure and promotes the beauty of northern Pakistan.

Azeeza Magh

Trekking & Sightseeing Guide

Born and raised in the Passu Valley, Hunza, Azeeza is a versatile guide specializing in high-altitude treks and immersive sightseeing tours. Known for her passion for adventure and storytelling, she has guided treks to the iconic K2 Base Camp and led countless tours showcasing the beauty, culture, and history of Gilgit-Baltistan. Azeeza’s dedication to safety, enjoyment, and cultural immersion makes her an exceptional guide for exploring northern Pakistan.

Our Philosophy — Passion, Safety, and Adventure

At Summit Experts, we believe in creating transformative travel experiences that connect people with nature and culture. Our team’s dedication to safety, sustainability, and authenticity drives everything we do.

Overview

About Expedition

Join us for a once-in-a-lifetime expedition to Nanga Parbat, the world’s ninth highest peak and one of the most formidable climbs on Earth. Our 23-days program takes you from Islamabad to the base camp and beyond, offering full support for your ascent of this awe-inspiring “Killer Mountain.” With seasoned guides, high-altitude porters, and a focus on safety and success, this expedition is designed for serious mountaineers seeking the ultimate test. Ready to write your name into Himalayan history? Get in touch to begin your journey.

Why This Tour?

  • Experienced expedition logistics team.
  • Strong local connections for hassle-free operations.
  • High-quality meals and equipment at base camp.
  • Professional support for both independent and guided climbers.
  • Reliable weather forecasting and emergency assistance.
  • Commitment to environmental sustainability and responsible tourism.

Itinerary

Day 1: Arrival in Islamabad

 The first day of the expedition involves arriving in Islamabad, the capital city of Pakistan. The team members will meet each other and go over the itinerary and logistics of the trip. The rest of the day is spent acclimatizing to the time zone and preparing for the journey ahead.

Day 2: Travel to Chilas

The team will depart Islamabad and travel by road to Chilas, a small town located in the Gilgit-Baltistan region of Pakistan. The journey takes around 12-14 hours and involves passing through several scenic valleys and mountain passes.

Day 3: Rest day in Chilas

The team will spend a day in Chilas, resting and acclimatizing to the higher altitude. They may also use this day to purchase any last-minute gear or supplies they need for the expedition.

Day 4: Travel to the Nanga Parbat Base Camp

The team will continue their journey by road to the base camp of Nanga Parbat, which is located at an altitude of approximately 4,200 meters. The road journey takes around 7-8 hours and is a challenging drive due to the rough terrain.

Day 5: Rest day at Base Camp

The team will spend a day at the base camp, setting up their tents and preparing for the climb ahead. They will also take a short acclimatization hike to a nearby hill to help their bodies adjust to the altitude.

Day 6-10: Acclimatization Period

The next few days will be spent on acclimatization hikes to higher elevations, in order to prepare the team members’ bodies for the climb. The hikes will be progressively longer and higher, with the team camping at higher elevations each night.

Day 11-18: Summit Push After the Acclimatization Period

The team will begin their summit push. They will move up the mountain in stages, establishing higher camps along the way. Each camp will be stocked with supplies and equipment, and the team will return to lower camps to rest and recover before moving higher.

Day 19-21: Descent After reaching the summit of Nanga Parbat

 The team will begin their descent down the mountain. They will follow the same path they took on the way up, taking their time to ensure a safe descent.

Day 22-23: Return to Chilas and Islamabad

The team will make their way back to Chilas and then to Islamabad, where they will debrief and celebrate the successful expedition. The rest of the time is spent relaxing and sightseeing in Islamabad, before departing for their home countries.

Itinerary

Day 1: Arrival in Islamabad

 The first day of the expedition involves arriving in Islamabad, the capital city of Pakistan. The team members will meet each other and go over the itinerary and logistics of the trip. The rest of the day is spent acclimatizing to the time zone and preparing for the journey ahead.

Day 2: Travel to Chilas

The team will depart Islamabad and travel by road to Chilas, a small town located in the Gilgit-Baltistan region of Pakistan. The journey takes around 12-14 hours and involves passing through several scenic valleys and mountain passes.

Day 3: Rest day in Chilas

The team will spend a day in Chilas, resting and acclimatizing to the higher altitude. They may also use this day to purchase any last-minute gear or supplies they need for the expedition.

Day 4: Travel to the Nanga Parbat Base Camp

The team will continue their journey by road to the base camp of Nanga Parbat, which is located at an altitude of approximately 4,200 meters. The road journey takes around 7-8 hours and is a challenging drive due to the rough terrain.

Day 5: Rest day at Base Camp

The team will spend a day at the base camp, setting up their tents and preparing for the climb ahead. They will also take a short acclimatization hike to a nearby hill to help their bodies adjust to the altitude.

Day 6-10: Acclimatization Period

The next few days will be spent on acclimatization hikes to higher elevations, in order to prepare the team members’ bodies for the climb. The hikes will be progressively longer and higher, with the team camping at higher elevations each night.

Day 22-23: Return to Chilas and Islamabad

Packing List

✔ Personal Gear
✔ Backpack: 50-60 liter capacity, lightweight with compression straps and ice axe loops.
✔ Daypack: 35-45 liter capacity for acclimatization hikes and approach treks.
✔ Duffel Bags: Durable, waterproof bags for gear transport; recommended 90-120 liters.

✔ Sleeping System
✔ Sleeping Bag: Rated to at least -20°C (-4°F); down-filled preferred for its warmth-to-weight ratio.
✔ Sleeping Pad: Inflatable or foam pad for insulation and comfort.
✔ Sleeping Bag Liner: Adds warmth and keeps the sleeping bag clean.

✔ Footwear
✔ High-Altitude Mountaineering Boots: Insulated double or triple boots suitable for 8000-meter peaks.
✔ Hiking Boots: Sturdy, well-broken-in boots for the trek to base camp.
✔ Camp Shoes: Lightweight footwear for use around camp.
✔ Gaiters: High-quality, waterproof gaiters to keep snow out of boots.
✔ Socks: Multiple pairs of thermal mountaineering socks and liner socks.

✔ Clothing
✔ Base Layers
✔ Thermal Underwear: Moisture-wicking, quick-drying tops and bottoms; merino wool or synthetic materials recommended.

✔ Mid Layers
✔ Insulated Jacket: Down or synthetic fill with a hood for added warmth.
✔ Soft Shell Jacket and Pants: Breathable, water-resistant layers for protection against wind and light precipitation.

✔ Outer Layers
✔ Hard Shell Jacket and Pants: Durable, waterproof, and breathable; Gore-Tex or similar material.
✔ Down Suit: Full-body suit designed for extreme cold at high altitudes.

✔ Additional Clothing
✔ Insulated Pants: Down or synthetic fill for high camps and summit attempts.
✔ Fleece or Soft Shell Pants: For added insulation during colder conditions.
✔ Gloves and Mittens: Layering system including liner gloves, insulated gloves, and expedition mittens.
✔ Hats: Warm beanie and balaclava for head and face protection.
✔ Neck Gaiter or Buff: Versatile protection for neck and face.

✔ Climbing Equipment
✔ Ice Axe: General mountaineering axe appropriate for your height.
✔ Crampons: 12-point steel crampons compatible with your boots.
✔ Climbing Harness: Lightweight, adjustable harness with gear loops.
✔ Helmet: UIAA-certified climbing helmet.
✔ Carabiners: Assorted locking and non-locking carabiners.
✔ Belay/Rappel Device: ATC-style device compatible with rope diameter.
✔ Ascender (Jumar): For fixed rope ascents.
✔ Prusik Cord: 6mm cord for safety backups and crevasse rescue.
✔ Trekking Poles: Adjustable, collapsible poles with snow baskets.

✔ Accessories
✔ Headlamp: High-output LED with extra batteries.
✔ Sunglasses: Category 4 lenses for high-altitude sun protection.
✔ Goggles: Anti-fog, UV-protective lenses for windy or snowy conditions.
✔ Water Bottles: Two 1-liter wide-mouth bottles; insulated covers recommended.
✔ Thermos: For hot drinks during cold conditions.
✔ Personal First Aid Kit: Including blister care, personal medications, and high-altitude remedies.
✔ Repair Kit: Duct tape, sewing kit, and repair materials for gear fixes.
✔ Stuff Sacks/Dry Bags: For organization and waterproofing gear.
✔ Camera: Optional, but ensure it’s durable and can withstand cold temperatures.
✔ Notebook and Pen: For journaling or note-taking.

✔ Personal Items
✔ Passport and Permits: Ensure all necessary documents are up-to-date and accessible.
✔ Insurance Documents: Proof of travel and evacuation insurance.
✔ Cash: For incidental expenses and tips.
✔ Toiletries: Biodegradable soap, toothbrush, toothpaste, floss, and other personal hygiene items.
✔ Sunscreen: SPF 50+ for high-altitude exposure.
✔ Lip Balm: With SPF protection.
✔ Towel: Lightweight, quick-drying.
✔ Earplugs: For restful sleep in communal settings.

Note: This list serves as a general guideline. Individual needs may vary based on personal
preferences and specific expedition requirements. Always consult with your expedition leader or

FAQs

01

Do I need experience in trekking for this trip?

+

No, this trip is suitable for moderate trekkers. While the trek to Fairy Meadows and Nanga Parbat Base Camp can be challenging, the pace is manageable for those with basic fitness levels. However, prior hiking experience is beneficial.

02

Is the trek suitable for families?

+

Yes, the trek can be enjoyed by families, though children should be in good physical condition and comfortable with hiking. The shorter treks around Fairy Meadows and Nanga Parbat Base Camp are generally accessible for younger trekkers, but we recommend checking the difficulty level before bringing young children.

03

What are the accommodation options during the trek?

+
  • Fairy Meadows: Stay options include Fairy Meadows Cottages, Raikot Sarai, or luxury tents depending on your preferences.
  • Chilas: There are options like Shangrila Hotel Chilas for premium stays and Indus Lodges for more budget-friendly choices.
  • Other Nights: Comfortable hotels like Hilton Hotel Besham or Sarai Hotel Naran for overnight stays on the return leg of the journey.
04

How difficult is the trek to Fairy Meadows and Nanga Parbat Base Camp?

+

The trek to Fairy Meadows is moderate, with a 2-3 hour walk from Tattu Village. For those opting for the Nanga Parbat Base Camp trek, it is a challenging 6-7 hour round trip with an elevation gain. You need good fitness and stamina for this section.

05

What is the weather like during the trek?

+

The weather can vary greatly depending on the season:

  • Spring/Autumn: Mild during the day, but cool at night.
  • Summer: Pleasant with warm days and cooler nights in the mountains.
  • Winter: Cold, with snow and icy conditions, especially at higher altitudes.
06

Is there any mobile network coverage in Fairy Meadows?

+

Mobile network coverage is limited in remote areas like Fairy Meadows. It’s advisable to inform family or friends in advance about your travel plans and expected availability.

07

What do I need to carry for the trek?

+

You should bring:

  • Comfortable trekking gear (shoes, backpack, clothing)
  • Personal essentials (ID, camera, water bottle, snacks)
  • Weather-appropriate clothing (depending on the season)
  • Sleeping bag and trekking poles (optional for camping and stability)
08

Will food and water be provided during the trek?

+

Yes, meals will be provided during the trek, including traditional Pakistani food at the camps and hotels. However, you should carry additional snacks like energy bars or trail mix for the journey.

09

Is there any health risk on this trek?

+

There is a low risk of altitude sickness since the trek does not involve very high altitudes. However, it’s always a good idea to be cautious and hydrate well. Carry any personal medication you may need, especially for allergies or other conditions.

10

How long is the total trek?

+

The entire trek to Fairy Meadows and Nanga Parbat Base Camp spans over 5-7 days, including travel time from Islamabad to the destination and back. You will spend multiple nights at Fairy Meadows, with time for exploration, relaxing, and optional additional trekking.

11

Can I customize my itinerary or add extra days?

+

Yes! This trip can be customized based on your preferences. You can add extra days for rest, exploration, or visit other scenic spots nearby. Please discuss with the tour operator for personalized adjustments.

12

Are there any optional activities during the trek?

+

Yes! You can opt for the Nanga Parbat Base Camp trek, exploring local villages, or simply relaxing and enjoying the scenic beauty of Fairy Meadows.

TOUR EXLCUSION/INCLUSION

01

What You Get?

+

Base Camp Services Only:

This package is for climbers who prefer to handle their own high-altitude logistics but need comprehensive support at base camp.

Includes:

  1. Permit Arrangements: Climbing permit for Nanga Parbat Peak, liaison officer, environmental fee.
  2. Accommodation & Meals: Hotels in Islamabad and Skardu (B/B), three meals per day at base camp.
  3. Transportation: Domestic flights (Islamabad-Skardu-Islamabad), jeep transport to Askole.
  4. Base Camp Setup: Spacious tents, dining tent, kitchen tent, toilet tent, solar charging.
  5. Kitchen Services: Professional base camp cook, kitchen staff, gas, utensils.
  6. Logistics & Communication: Porters for group equipment, base camp internet and communication setup.
  7. Support Staff: Liaison officer, assistant staff, permit paperwork, briefing/debriefing.
  8. Weather Updates: Regular weather forecast updates.
  9. Medical Support: Basic first aid kit at base camp.
  10. Garbage Management: Waste disposal as per environmental regulations.
  11. Security Clearance: Coordination with local authorities.
  12. BC Generator: Generator for charging electronic devices.
  13. Mess Tent Facilities: Comfortable dining arrangements.
  14. Personal Tent at BC: Individual sleeping tents.
  15. Dining & Lounge Facilities: Proper seating arrangement.
  16. Porterage: For group and personal luggage to base camp.
  17. Satellite Phone Access: Available on a per-minute charge.
  18. Insurance of Staff: Coverage for base camp staff.
  19. Assistance with Customs Clearance: For expedition cargo.
  20. Photography & Documentation Assistance: Support for media requirements.
  21. Expedition Briefing & Debriefing: Assistance with official processes.

Full Board Services:

This package includes base camp services plus high-altitude logistics for climbers needing full support.

Includes:

  1. Everything in Base Camp Services, plus:
  2. High-Altitude Equipment & Support: Fixed ropes, anchors, climbing permits, route fixing costs.
  3. High-Altitude One to One Guide (HAGs): 1 Pakistani climbing guide per member.
  4. High-Altitude Meals & Gas: Pre-packed meals for higher camps, stoves, gas refills.
  5. Oxygen Support (if required at extra cost): Oxygen cylinders, mask, and regulator rental.
  6. Rescue Assistance: Coordination for emergency evacuation and medical assistance.
  7. Personal Climbing Sherpa (if required at extra cost).
  8. Tent at Higher Camps: Provision of tents for high-altitude camps.
  9. Sleeping Mats & Cooking Equipment: For high camps.
  10. Rope Fixing Charges: Shared costs for rope fixing on the route.
  11. Load Carrying to High Camps: Distribution of essential supplies.
  12. Climbing Permit Coordination: Smooth permit processing.
  13. Medical Kit for High Altitude: Advanced first aid provisions.
  14. Weather Forecasting Services: Specialized weather updates for summit push.
  15. Daily Communication with BC & Team Coordination.
  16. Garbage Collection at High Camps: Waste disposal according to environmental regulations.
  17. Summit Push Planning & Strategy Assistance.
  18. High Camp Fuel & Stoves.
  19. Safety Equipment & Coordination for Team Members.
02

What You Don’t?

+
  • International airfare to/from Pakistan.
  • Personal climbing gear (boots, harness, ice axe, crampons, etc.).
  • Personal insurance (medical, travel, evacuation, etc.).
  • Extra hotel nights in case of delays (bad weather, permit issues, etc.).
  • Additional meals in cities beyond itinerary.
  • Personal expenses (laundry, phone calls, internet, extra snacks, drinks, souvenirs, etc.).
  • Emergency evacuation costs (helicopter rescue, medical treatment, hospitalization, etc.).
  • Summit bonus for high-altitude porters and staff (recommended but not included).
  • Oxygen equipment (can be arranged at additional cost).
  • Personal climbing Sherpa (can be arranged at additional cost).
  • Any costs arising due to natural disasters, political instability, or unexpected itinerary changes.
  • Costs due to delays in flights or road transport.
  • Any other services not mentioned in the inclusions.

Overview

About This Trip

Step back in time and immerse yourself in the rich history and culture of Peshawar, a city known for its ancient traditions and architectural wonders. This full-day tour begins with a visit to the Peshawar Museum, home to an impressive collection of Gandhara art and Buddhist relics. Wander through the bustling Qissa Khwani Bazaar, where you’ll experience the heart of Peshawari life with traditional tea houses and local handicrafts.

Explore the grandeur of Sethi House Museum, a beautifully preserved 19th-century mansion, followed by a visit to the stunning Mohabbat Khan Mosque, a marvel of Mughal architecture. For a panoramic view of the city, we’ll stop by Bala Hisar Fort, admired from the outside.

After a delicious lunch at a local restaurant, enjoy an optional visit to the legendary Khyber Pass (subject to security clearance), one of the most historic trade routes in the world, followed by a stop at Bab-e-Khyber and Jamrud Fort.

This day trip provides a unique blend of history, culture, and breathtaking landscapes, making it an unforgettable journey through Peshawar’s past and present.

Why This Tour?

✅ Historical Significance – Explore Peshawar’s rich history, from Gandhara art to Mughal architecture, offering an in-depth understanding of the city’s evolution.
✅ Cultural Immersion – Walk through Qissa Khwani Bazaar, the “Bazaar of Storytellers,” and experience authentic Peshawari culture, including traditional tea houses and local handicrafts.
✅ Architectural Wonders – Visit iconic landmarks like Sethi House Museum and Mohabbat Khan Mosque, showcasing the beautiful architectural heritage of the city.
✅ Stunning Views – Admire the city from the historic Bala Hisar Fort and, if security allows, explore the Khyber Pass for breathtaking mountain views and a glimpse of tribal culture.
✅ Culinary Experience – Enjoy a traditional Peshawari lunch, including Chapli Kebab and Karahi, giving you a true taste of the region.
✅ Optional Adventure – If available, visit Jamrud Fort and Bab-e-Khyber, enhancing your trip with an exploration of historic forts and gates that mark the entrance to the Khyber Pass

Itinerary

Your guide will pick you up from your hotel, and we’ll start exploring the historic and culturally rich city of Peshawar.

Peshawar Museum

Visit the Peshawar Museum, home to an extensive collection of Gandhara art, Buddhist relics, and artifacts from various eras of history.

Qissa Khwani Bazaar

Explore the famous Qissa Khwani Bazaar, also known as the “Bazaar of Storytellers.” This historic marketplace is filled with traditional tea houses, local handicrafts, and authentic Peshawari culture.

Sethi House Museum

Step inside Sethi House, a beautifully preserved mansion from the 19th century showcasing the rich architectural heritage of Peshawar.

Mohabbat Khan Mosque

Visit the Mohabbat Khan Mosque, a stunning 17th-century Mughal-era mosque known for its intricate tile work and grand courtyard.

Bala Hisar Fort (Outside View Only)

A historic fortress with a commanding view of the city. While entry is restricted, you can still admire its impressive structure from the outside.

Lunch at a Traditional Restaurant

Enjoy a delicious lunch featuring Peshawari cuisine, such as:

Namak Mandi – Famous for its traditional Chapli Kebabs and Karahi

Shiraz Ronaq – A well-known spot offering a variety of local and Pakistani dishes

Khyber Pass (Optional, Subject to Security Clearance)

If permitted, we can drive towards the legendary Khyber Pass, a historic trade route that connects Pakistan to Afghanistan. This area holds immense historical significance, offering breathtaking mountain views and a glimpse into tribal culture.

Bab-e-Khyber (Khyber Gate)

A symbolic gateway to the Khyber Pass, this monument marks the entrance to one of the most famous passes in the world.

Jamrud Fort (Optional Stop Near Khyber Pass)

If time allows, we can visit Jamrud Fort, a historic fortress that played a crucial role in the region’s past.

Drop-off at Hotel

After an exciting day exploring the cultural heart of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, your guide will drop you back at your hotel.

(Tour Starts and Ends in Peshawar – If some other city additional Charges will apply)

Qissa Khwani Bazaar

Explore the famous Qissa Khwani Bazaar, also known as the “Bazaar of Storytellers.” This historic marketplace is filled with traditional tea houses, local handicrafts, and authentic Peshawari culture.

Sethi House Museum

Step inside Sethi House, a beautifully preserved mansion from the 19th century showcasing the rich architectural heritage of Peshawar.

Mohabbat Khan Mosque

Visit the Mohabbat Khan Mosque, a stunning 17th-century Mughal-era mosque known for its intricate tile work and grand courtyard.

Bala Hisar Fort (Outside View Only)

A historic fortress with a commanding view of the city. While entry is restricted, you can still admire its impressive structure from the outside.

Lunch at a Traditional Restaurant

Enjoy a delicious lunch featuring Peshawari cuisine, such as:

Namak Mandi – Famous for its traditional Chapli Kebabs and Karahi

Shiraz Ronaq – A well-known spot offering a variety of local and Pakistani dishes

Khyber Pass (Optional, Subject to Security Clearance)

If permitted, we can drive towards the legendary Khyber Pass, a historic trade route that connects Pakistan to Afghanistan. This area holds immense historical significance, offering breathtaking mountain views and a glimpse into tribal culture.

Bab-e-Khyber (Khyber Gate)

A symbolic gateway to the Khyber Pass, this monument marks the entrance to one of the most famous passes in the world.

Jamrud Fort (Optional Stop Near Khyber Pass)

If time allows, we can visit Jamrud Fort, a historic fortress that played a crucial role in the region’s past.

Drop-off at Hotel

After an exciting day exploring the cultural heart of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, your guide will drop you back at your hotel.

(Tour Starts and Ends in Peshawar – If some other city additional Charges will apply)

Key Information

  • Destinations Covered: Peshawar Museum, Qissa Khwani Bazaar, Sethi House Museum, Mohabbat Khan Mosque, Bala Hisar Fort (outside view), Bab-e-Khyber, and optional stops at Khyber Pass & Jamrud Fort (subject to security clearance).
  • Tour Duration: Full-day tour (8–10 hours).
  • Best Season: Year-round (Spring & Autumn offer the best weather).
  • Difficulty Level: Easy – Suitable for all ages, with moderate walking.
  • Starting & Ending Point: Peshawar (Hotel pickup & drop-off included).
  • Entry Requirements: No special permits required for the city; Khyber Pass visit is subject to security clearance.
  • Meals: Traditional Peshawari lunch at a local restaurant.
  • Transport: Private vehicle with driver and English-speaking guide.
  • Additional Costs: Entry fees (if applicable), personal expenses, and optional purchases from bazaars.
  • Customizations: Available upon request (special pickup from another city may incur additional charges).

FAQs

01

What is included in the Peshawar Day Trip?

+

The tour includes hotel pick-up and drop-off, private transportation, a professional English-speaking guide, and visits to all listed attractions. Meals, entry fees (if applicable), and personal expenses are not included.

02

How long does the tour last?

+

The trip lasts approximately 8 to 10 hours, depending on the time spent at each location and traffic conditions.

03

Is this tour suitable for all age groups?

+

Yes, the tour is designed for all ages with moderate walking involved. However, if you have mobility concerns, please inform us in advance for necessary arrangements.

04

What should I wear for the trip?

+

Peshawar has a warm climate most of the year. Wear comfortable clothing, closed-toe walking shoes, and carry sunglasses and sunscreen. In winter, bring a light jacket for cooler mornings and evenings.

05

Are meals included in the package?

+

Lunch at a traditional Peshawari restaurant is included. However, snacks, beverages, and additional meals are not covered.

06

Can I shop during the tour?

+

Yes! You will have time to explore Qissa Khwani Bazaar, where you can buy local handicrafts, spices, and traditional Peshawari items.

07

Will there be a guide during the tour?

+

Yes, a professional English-speaking guide will accompany you throughout the tour, providing insights into the city's rich history and culture.

08

Can I visit the Khyber Pass?

+

The visit to the Khyber Pass and Jamrud Fort is optional and subject to security clearance. If permitted, we can drive to Bab-e-Khyber for a glimpse of this historic route.

09

Is the tour wheelchair/stroller accessible?

+

Most locations are accessible, but some heritage sites may have stairs or uneven paths. Please inform us in advance so we can arrange assistance.

10

What happens in case of bad weather?

+

The tour operates in all weather conditions. In extreme situations, alternative arrangements may be suggested.

Privacy Policy

Privacy Policy

Summit Experts Adventure Tours (“Summit Experts,” “we,” “us,” “our”) is committed to protecting your privacy. This Privacy Policy explains how we collect, use, disclose, and safeguard your information when you visit our website, www.thesummitexperts.com (“Website”). By using our Website, you agree to the terms outlined in this policy. If you do not agree, please do not use the Website.

  1. Information We Collect

    We collect personal data from you in the following ways:

    • Contact Forms: Your name, WhatsApp number, and email address when you inquire about our services.
    • Newsletter Sign-ups: Your name and email address.
    • Bookings and Transactions: Information necessary to process your tour reservations, including payment details (processed securely by third-party providers).
    • Website Analytics: IP addresses, browser type, visit duration, and interactions to improve user experience.
  2. How We Use Your Information

    We use your information to:

    • Process bookings and respond to inquiries.
    • Improve our Website and services.
    • Send updates, promotions, and newsletters (with your consent).
    • Monitor and analyze usage trends to enhance customer experience.
    • Comply with legal obligations.
  3. Cookies and Tracking Technologies

    Like many websites, we use cookies to enhance user experience. These cookies:

    • Help recognize repeat visitors.
    • Store preferences for future visits.
    • Track website traffic patterns.

    You can modify your browser settings to decline cookies, but this may affect your ability to fully use our Website.

  4. Data Protection and Security

    We take reasonable security measures to protect your personal information, including encryption and secure servers. However, no online transmission is 100% secure. Use our Website at your own risk.

  5. Sharing of Information

    We do not sell or rent your personal information. However, we may share data with:

    • Service Providers: Payment processors, booking platforms, and marketing partners that help us operate our business.
    • Legal Authorities: If required by law or to protect our legal rights.
    • Business Transfers: If Summit Experts undergoes a merger, sale, or asset transfer, your data may be included.
  6. Your Rights (GDPR & Other Regulations)

    If you are in the EU or other jurisdictions with data privacy laws, you have rights, including:

    • Access to your data and the right to correct or delete it.
    • Objecting to data processing or requesting data portability.
    • Withdrawing consent for marketing emails (unsubscribe option available).
    • Requesting deletion of your data by contacting us.
  7. Children’s Privacy

    Our services are not directed to individuals under 18. We do not knowingly collect data from minors. If we discover such data, we will delete it promptly.

  8. External Links

    Our Website may contain links to third-party websites. We are not responsible for their privacy practices, so we recommend reviewing their policies before providing any information.

  9. Changes to This Privacy Policy

    We may update this Privacy Policy from time to time. Any changes will be reflected by updating the effective date at the top. We encourage you to review this policy periodically.

Our group of five Thai friends explored Skardu, Hunza, Passu, and Gilgit at the peak of blossom season. Guided by the company’s CEO, Shah, whose extensive expertise in hiking and expeditions was evident, we found ourselves on a well-planned yet refreshingly adaptable journey. We appreciated how our tour leader went above and beyond, recommending exclusive experiences—from an insightful cultural visit to a local Pakistani home to a glacier trek using a unique route. Unlike standard itineraries, this allowed us to truly get up close and touch the glacier, all while ensuring our safety with expert guidance. One of the highlights was our trek to Fairy Meadows. With hours of hiking ahead, our guide was highly attentive, carefully assessing the natural conditions and our group’s well-being, which made us feel completely safe every step of the way. I already can't wait to return to Pakistan in summer, autumn, and beyond! 😊 A little tip for fellow travelers: If you plan to visit areas that require trekking and hiking, I highly recommend familiarizing yourself with the terrain beforehand. You can always check with the Summit Experts Adventure Tours team about the travel conditions—just to be prepared, not to opt out! The beauty of northern Pakistan is absolutely worth the effort.

A Journey to Remember
I just returned from an incredible month-long adventure in northern Pakistan with Summit Experts Adventure Tours. We trekked through some of the most breathtaking regions: Skardu, Hunza, Shimshal Village, and made our way to Shimshal Pass, ending with the exhilarating summit of Manglik Sar (6050m). From the very first moment, I knew I was in the hands of true professionals. The entire trip was perfectly organized, from the logistics to safety measures. But what truly made this experience stand out was the team. Every single person was warm, supportive, and treated me like family. Over the course of the trek, they all became a second family to me, and I genuinely feel like I’ve made lifelong friends. The beauty of the Karakoram combined with the knowledge, passion, and dedication of the Summit Experts team made this adventure unforgettable. I felt supported, safe, and inspired every single day. I don’t add pictures, because you MUST visit and see all the beauty of Pakistan with your own eyes. Nothing can compare to standing there in person, taking in the vastness and the majesty of the Karakoram range. Thanks to the expertise of Summit Experts, I felt safe and supported every step of the way. The team’s passion for the mountains and commitment to making sure each trekker has the best possible experience is what really sets them apart. This wasn’t just a trek—it was an unforgettable journey, and I already can’t wait to return. I’m already thinking about next year and planning to do even more trekking in Pakistan. There’s so much more to explore, and I wouldn’t want to do it with anyone else but Summit Experts. If you’re considering an adventure in Pakistan, I cannot recommend this company enough. Beyond the ordinary
It took me some time to find the right words to capture the incredible memories we created during our trip to northern Pakistan this April—blossom season at its absolute best! The breathtaking views, the warmth of the people, and the richness of the culture left a lasting impression on me, all made even more special by the Summit Experts Adventure Tours team. Their approach was not just professional but also incredibly humble and flexible, ensuring we had an unforgettable experience. Our group of five Thai friends explored Skardu, Hunza, Passu, and Gilgit at the peak of blossom season. Guided by the company’s CEO, Shah, whose extensive expertise in hiking and expeditions was evident, we found ourselves on a well-planned yet refreshingly adaptable journey. We appreciated how our tour leader went above and beyond, recommending exclusive experiences—from an insightful cultural visit to a local Pakistani home to a glacier trek using a unique route. Unlike standard itineraries, this allowed us to truly get up close and touch the glacier, all while ensuring our safety with expert guidance. One of the highlights was our trek to Fairy Meadows. With hours of hiking ahead, our guide was highly attentive, carefully assessing the natural conditions and our group’s well-being, which made us feel completely safe every step of the way. I already can't wait to return to Pakistan in summer, autumn, and beyond! 😊 A little tip for fellow travelers: If you plan to visit areas that require trekking and hiking, I highly recommend familiarizing yourself with the terrain beforehand. You can always check with the Summit Experts Adventure Tours team about the travel conditions—just to be prepared, not to opt out! The beauty of northern Pakistan is absolutely worth the effort.
